newsitem.title: USA: Boston agency to be fined over $100,000 - report.
newsitem.headline: Boston agency to be fined over $100,000 - report.

text.p: The Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination is expected to announce later Monday that it is fining the Boston Housing Authority more than $100,000 in a case of racial discrimination, the Boston Globe reported.

John Love, a black security guard who lives in the Charlestown Housing Development, filed more than dozen complaints and an emergency request for transfer to another BHA-owned apartment after finding flyers advertising Ku Klux Klan meetings on his door, epithet-filled graffitti on the hallways of his buildings and having visitors to his home called "nigger" by his neighbors, the newspaper said.
But the Boston Housing Authority never responded to any of his complaints, MCAD said.
According to the newspaper, MCAD plans to order BHA to pay Love more than $100,000 and has ordered it to pay an additional $10,000 civil fine and transfer Love to another housing complex.
BHA Administrator Sandra Henriquez told the newspaper she is considering appealing the decision.
